title: What Was the Deal With the Hatfields and McCoys?
summary: Josh and Chuck cover the Hatfield and McCoy feud, the late-19th-century Appalachian clan conflict along the Tug River on the West Virginia-Kentucky border. They trace both families' origins, the Civil War roots of the conflict, Asa Harmon McCoy's killing, the Floyd Hatfield hog-theft trial, the Bill Staton and election-day killings, the Perry Klein and Frank Phillips bounty-hunting phase, the New Year's Day 1888 attack on the McCoy home, Ellison Mounts's hanging, the eventual truce, and the feud's afterlife in pop culture, medicine, and World War II publicity. The episode opens with concert tour announcements and closes with a listener mail segment and sign-off.

segments.title: Tour dates and ticket announcement
segments.summary: Hosts announce Spring Has Sprung tour dates and direct listeners to the live site for tickets.

segments.title: Opening banter and topic setup
segments.summary: Hosts banter and introduce the Hatfield and McCoy feud, noting Jerry's claimed relation to one family and the 1990s-era TV miniseries.

segments.title: Origins of the Hatfield and McCoy families
segments.summary: The families' immigration roots (Hatfields from England, McCoys from Scotland via Ireland), their settling in the Tug River Valley, and the personalities of patriarchs Devil Anse Hatfield and Randall McCoy, including the wealth gap between them.

segments.title: Civil War roots and Asa Harmon McCoy's death
segments.summary: Confederate loyalties in the valley, the Logan Wildcats militia, Asa Harmon McCoy's Union service and fight with Devil Anse, his killing of a Confederate friend, and his murder by the Logan Wildcats after returning home.

segments.title: Floyd Hatfield hog theft trial
segments.summary: The pig theft accusation by Randall McCoy against Floyd Hatfield, the rigged-looking jury of six Hatfields and six McCoys, the verdict of acquittal after juror Selkirk McCoy's vote, and Randall's anger.

segments.title: Escalating killings: Bill Staton, Paris McCoy and election day violence
segments.summary: Bill Staton Jr. shoots Paris McCoy and is executed by Sam McCoy; later, three McCoy sons are stabbed and Ellison Hatfield is killed on election day; the McCoy sons are kidnapped and executed by Hatfields.

segments.title: Perry Klein, governor involvement, and Frank Phillips
segments.summary: Attorney Perry Klein's role and his appeal to Kentucky's governor, the bounties on Hatfield men, bounty hunter Frank Phillips's raids and executions, and the interstate standoff that reached the Supreme Court.

segments.title: New Year's Day attack, trials, and Ellison Mounts's hanging
segments.summary: The January 1 attack on the McCoy home that killed Calvin and Alafair McCoy and beat Sarah McCoy; the 1889 trials with eight life sentences and one hanging of Ellison Mounts; Randall's subdued later life.

segments.title: Truce, legacy, pop culture, medical theory, and World War II
segments.summary: The truce and the roughly two dozen deaths over eleven years, Devil Anse's later life, the feud in movies and cartoons, a proposed genetic explanation (von Hippel-Lindau disease), Life magazine's World War II spread, and the Frank Phillips and John Hatfield romance backstories.

segments.title: Listener mail from Jennifer Hardy
segments.summary: A listener from Illinois praises the show and says she listens daily; hosts read the email and explain how to contact the show.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts direct listeners to the website for more information.
